item.title: Wisconsin Assembly passes deals on PFAS, SNAP funding
item.description: Capping off a contentious week of floor sessions that saw tempers flare as lawmakers raced to adjourn for the year, the state Assembly passed two measures tied to hard-fought deals about food assistance and cleaning up PFAS. The post Wisconsin Assembly passes deals on PFAS, SNAP funding appeared first on WPR.

item.title: UW-Madison’s public affairs school receives $30M honoring Herb Kohl, finds new home
item.description: The gift from Herb Kohl Philanthropies will turn the university’s Music Hall into Herb Kohl Hall and also help support school programming. The post UW-Madison’s public affairs school receives $30M honoring Herb Kohl, finds new home appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Snowy season boosts northern Wisconsin tourism, but winters are becoming unreliable
item.description: Wisconsin feels more like winter than it has in years. The weather has been colder than normal so far, and big storms dumped a lot of snow on the state. That’s boosted winter businesses and events that have struggled with recent warm winters. The post Snowy season boosts northern Wisconsin tourism, but winters are becoming unreliable appeared first on WPR.

item.title: US Attorney General endorses call to make tribe repay town in Northwoods roads dispute
item.description: U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi said she’s willing to work with a Republican congressman who wants to force a northern Wisconsin tribe to reimburse the town of Lac du Flambeau for payments to access roads. The post US Attorney General endorses call to make tribe repay town in Northwoods roads dispute appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Kenosha’s Eagles Club has been a staple of the community for nearly 100 years. It could soon be demolished.
item.description: Co-owner Dan Madrigrano said the "rough estimates" to repair the building are currently around $4 to $5 million. The post Kenosha’s Eagles Club has been a staple of the community for nearly 100 years. It could soon be demolished. appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Sturgeon spearing season ending early on Lake Winnebago
item.description: The sturgeon spearing season on Lake Winnebago will end Monday afternoon, after spearers got close to hitting the harvest cap for adult female sturgeon. The post Sturgeon spearing season ending early on Lake Winnebago appeared first on WPR.

item.title: How to disconnect from your phone
item.description: A psychologist visited WPR's "The Larry Meiller Show" to troubleshoot ideas on how we can cut back on our screen time. The post How to disconnect from your phone appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Athletes with ties to Wisconsin bring home gold at 2026 Winter Olympics
item.description: Wisconsin had its fair share of athletes representing the United States at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan, Italy. Including Jordan Stolz who took home two gold medals and one silver. The post Athletes with ties to Wisconsin bring home gold at 2026 Winter Olympics appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Matt Walker leaves UW-River Falls after national championship to coach at Drake University
item.description: After a transformational 15 years as head coach of the University of Wisconsin-River Falls football team, Matt Walker is leaving for Drake University. The post Matt Walker leaves UW-River Falls after national championship to coach at Drake University appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Wisconsin’s state Assembly adjourned without changes to school funding
item.description: For weeks, it looked like a deal might be struck between legislative Republicans and Gov. Tony Evers to use some of the state’s $2.5 billion surplus to provide both tax relief and money for schools. But those talks fell apart early last week. The post Wisconsin’s state Assembly adjourned without changes to school funding appeared first on WPR.
